fixes.explanation: Silas is a fun name to throw out, friend, but Demetrius never says it. He has gathered the craftsmen and the workmen in related trades (Acts 19:25). He points at just one man and says, "…this Paul has persuaded a great number of people to turn away." (Acts 19:26)

That's right. Alexander motions for silence so he can make his defense (Acts 19:33). Then "…when they realized that he was a Jew, they all shouted in unison for about two hours: “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”" (Acts 19:34) The verse records two hours of the same shout.

That's right. "After he had said this, he dismissed the assembly." (Acts 19:41) First the clerk quieted the crowd (Acts 19:35). Then he spoke, and then he dismissed them. Before that, they had shouted for about two hours (Acts 19:34).
